prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1446; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a parking lot collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck while stationary. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of the incident. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage period.

Entry 3: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene. The responding officer's notes also match the other parties' accounts of where the vehicles came to rest.

Entry 4: Photographs taken at the scene confirm several details of the impact. The damage to the vehicle is mostly consistent with the described collision, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known.

Entry 5: No independent witnesses have come forward. The available evidence rests on the photos, the police report, and the parties' statements.

Entry 6: The claimant gave the same account in every conversation, including the recorded statement taken through counsel. The details have not shifted between contacts.

Entry 7: Medical records show a whiplash-type injury, which is a plausible result for a collision of this kind. Records also note a minor strain to the same area several years ago that healed fully. Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the claimant improved.

Entry 8: Reserve reviewed in light of the medical course and the damage estimate. Claim remains open pending final medical documentation and counsel's demand package.
